issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The change touches only the training-label transform. It switches from uniform rank scores to normal (Gaussian) rank scores via norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n). The arguments stay strictly inside (0,1), so the result is always finite. It uses no test labels and no file access.

No bug. Spearman correlation depends only on the order of the predictions, and the existing mu/sd standardisation still applies. One thing to note: the SVR epsilon=0.05 now sits on a scale with sd of about 1 instead of about 0.29. In effect this narrows the epsilon tube relative to the data spread. That is a modelling choice, not an error.
The gain is 0.4830 - 0.4824 = 0.0006, roughly 0.06 noise sd from a single run on each side. This is well within noise, so rejecting is correct.
Recomputed z = 0.0006 / (0.0070*sqrt(1/1+1/1)) ≈ 0.061. The harness value of 0.056 fits once the 4-decimal rounding of the two means is allowed for (a true difference of about 0.00055).
